why: superseded by the v3 redraw after rule 1 (DOI prefix 10.1016) was removed from eligibility; this sample was drawn from the rule-1 eligible pool (commit 1a41053)

calibration_sample.rng: python random.Random(rng_seed); strata sorted by paper_id, then random.sample() per stratum, then shuffle() of the 50
calibration_sample.pool_definition: eligible == True (eligibility.py) AND abstract_source in openalex|semantic_scholar AND abstract non-empty
calibration_sample.excluded_no_abstract_basis: eligible rows only; ineligible rows are counted under excluded_ineligible

pool_exclusion_by_full_list_third.basis: Thirds are cut on the POOL, so these rates say how much that choice mattered. Equal rates mean cutting before or after the filters was the same decision; divergent rates mean pool exclusion is rank-correlated and the pool cut sits at a different paper than the full-list cut would.

calibration_sample.note: kappa computed on this sample is a kappa ON A STRATIFIED SAMPLE. It is not an estimate of kappa over the full ranked corpus, because the top third is deliberately oversampled 2:1 to put enough includes in the denominator for include-recall to mean anything. `stratum` is carried on every sample row so a later analysis can reweight. labels_TODO.csv omits stratum, rank and every seed-linkage column: a rater who can see how the pipeline ranked a paper is not an independent rater, and the resulting kappa would measure agreement with the ranking instead of agreement about the criteria.
